questions.question: Which language would you use for a CLI?

options.label: Rust
options.description: Compiles to a fast, single static binary with strong type safety and excellent CLI crates like clap.

options.label: Go
options.description: Simple language with fast builds, easy cross-compilation, and a solid standard library for CLI tools.

options.label: Swift
options.description: Modern, expressive language with great macOS/Apple platform integration via ArgumentParser.

options.label: Vim
options.description: Modal, keyboard-driven editor that runs anywhere a terminal does and stays out of your way.

options.label: Emacs
options.description: Endlessly extensible Lisp environment where the editor is a programmable operating layer.

options.label: VS Code
options.description: Graphical editor with a huge extension ecosystem and strong out-of-the-box language support.
